MRI of left Knee with 
-3-Plane Loc LT, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Ax T2 FS, Ax DWI B800, Screen Save, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, ADC (10^-6 mm?s):[DATE] [TIME]



> Some osteophytes and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage of left knee, reflecting osteoarthritis
  Wearing of articular cartilage and tiny subchondral cyst over patellar ridge, reflecting grade 3-4 chondromalacia (Srs/Img: [ID].
> Patellar enthesophyte; tendinosis of quadriceps tendon and iliotibial band.
> Mild fat stranding over suprapatellar fat pad, R/O suprapatellar fat pad impingement syndrome
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
  Lobulated hyperintensity foci with internal septums in retrocondylar region of left knee, reflecting retrocondylar bursitis/ gastrocnemius bursitis.
  Small Baker's cyst and popliteus bursitis.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity. 
> Mild interstitial increased signal intensity of ACL on F/S T2WI, in favor of degeneration.
> PCL, medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Subcutaneous infiltration over left anterior knee.

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee, more prominent at patellofemoral joint with focal grade 3-4 chondromalacia. 
2. Mild synovitis of left knee with patellar plicae and small Baker's cyst and retrocondylar bursitis/ gastrocnemius bursitis. (Srs/Img: [ID]; 6/9-14)
4. Grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration or meniscal vascularity.
5. Mild subcutaneous edema over left anterior knee.
6. Suprapatellar fat pad impingement syndrome and tendinosis of quadriceps tendon.
7. Degeneration of ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and physical examination

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:

Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 6 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Normal MRI of the left knee.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Gonalgia en estudio.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales dentro de límites normales.
El menisco lateral es de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Aumento de señal del meniscocapsular del cuerno posterior y cuerpo del menisco medial, podría
representar lesión parcial regional, no desplazada. El resto del menisco medial sin alteraciones
significativas.
Cartílagos los compartimentos femorotibiales y de la tróclea femoral sin alteraciones.
Úlceras condrales de espesor total con cambios óseos secundarios del vértice y faceta lateral de
la rótula.
No hay evidente derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos patológicos.
Aumento de señal de la inserción distal del tendón cuadricipital y de la inserción proximal del
tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda
iliotibial dentro de límites normales.
Leve aumento de señal de las partes blandas entre la banda iliotibial y el cóndilo femoral lateral.
Impresión:
Signos de una lesión meniscocapsular al menos parcial del cuerno posterior y parte del cuerpo del
menisco medial, correlacionar con clínica.
Condropatía lesiones grado 4 de la rótula.
Tendinosis cuadricipital distal y rotuliana proximal. Probables fenómenos de fricción de la banda
iliotibial
